# PREAMBLE FOR AUTHORS

::: {.callout-warning}
## I beg your attention please

This QMD script is a template/example. Among its characteristics :

-   A **auto-foldable TOC** is active (upper left panel)
-   Sections are **numbered** and **anchored** ([example](#purpose-of-this-session))
-   Source code is **embedded** (`</> Code` button in the upper-right corner)
-   The `flatly` **CSS theme** is applied
-   Lightbox available for images and plots
-   Width is **filled** with content **to the right** (up to 1600px by default)
-   The rendered HTML is **self-contained** (all dependencies/images are embedded in the HTML output)
-   Code chunks have a (context-dependent) **background color** and a blue (#31BAE9) **left border**
-   Chunk code **lines** are automatically **numbered**
-   Long code **lines** are automatically **wrapped** (this should not be actually in use due to the high grid:body-width value, but just in case you prefer deactivating it...).
-   Code **annotation** is active and is recommended. Same [example](#soupx-helper-function)
-   **Callout collapsing** is available and recommended to hide callouts corresponding to **special cases** : **questions, and answers** (roughly).
    -   It is **inactive** by default (can be activated per-callout using `collapse="true"`)
-   Code chunk **output collapsing** is available thanks to a knitr hook provided in the HTML header. It is useful in some cases (like, hiding a UMAP output for which an intuition question was asked), but please do not overuse it as it may make some trainees loose the track...
    -   It is **inactive** by default (can be activated per-chunk using the Quarto R chunk comment `#| attr.output: '.details summary="Show output"'`)
-   An HTML code is provided in the HTML header to force the **drawing of HTML tables border** (only useful if one intend to use basic HTML tables rather than kable, by ex)? An example is provided [here](#tldr-for-authors)
-   A "hack" of callouts is used to **color sections/chunks**, depending on their purpose. See [here](#what-to-run).
-   In this template, R chunks always include the QMD `#| label:` and `#| filename:` with the **same text value**. This is a trick used to display the chunk name in the output, as a header for each evaluated chunk. This is useful to use as anchors to help trainees keep in synch between the projected output and the QMD source on their own screen. While using this trick is not mandatory, it is highly recommended.

:::

# Purpose of this session {#purpose-of-this-session}

>Here is an example of a training session preamble : a very synthetic description of the upcoming content, with a specific warning from the very first training session ("Preproc.1").<br>The targets of this section are the students.


This file describes the different steps to perform the **first part** of the **single cell RNAseq** data analysis training course for the **EB3I n1 2026**, covering these steps :

-   **Load** a single cell raw counts **matrix**
-   **Remove** barcodes from **empty droplets**
-   **Estimate** and remove **ambient RNA** contamination *("soup")*

::: {.callout-important}
## An important notice

-   These early (but mandatory) steps of the analysis are not covered by the renowned, higher-level analysis frameworks like **Seurat** nor **scran/scater**.
-   Thus, we will write/use a certain amount of **lines of code**, some of which of a higher complexity for R beginners.
-   **Newcomer, do not fear** !
    -   While you are **welcome to try** writing some by yourself, depending on your R knowledge and self-confidence in it ...
    -   ... you do not have to know [**how**]{.underline} these code work ...
    -   ... thus you **should not feel ashamed** copy-pasting the pre-written code hereafter ...
    -   ... but in both cases, please try **your best understanding** [**what**]{.underline} these code do, and even more, [**why**]{.underline} !
    -   In this purpose, you may use whatever **help** you can **by** **searching**.

:::

::: {.callout-note icon="true" style="background: lightblue"}
As this is a template, most chunks here will not be evaluated. They will be
only where their output matters for the following chunks.

:::

Data should be retrieved and loaded from a Zenodo repo, and corresponding identifiers will thus change in function of the training session block (see a list in TL;DR 2)

In case we may lose the internet connection to Zenodo (it happened in 2025 when CloudFlare went down!), a "local" backup is available on the IFB instance [**NOTE : WILL** be available : it has not yet been moved from the 2025 location for the moment, due to cluster being down and 2026 project id not yet defined and opened]

- How the "local" (ie, on the IFB cluster) working dir tree is shaped and built

## Fetching some input data

### The loading functions

We created 2 functions to handle two cases :

1. When we have access to Zenodo and can **download** the input data to the students project directory. [**[But we won't thanks to AIs]**]{style="color:red"}

2. When we lose the access to Zenodo, we can **copy** a local backup (from the IFB cluster)

In the hypothetical case we lose the internet connection : all is lost, even the access to the cluster is impossible !

The code of these functions is :

-   available in the `/shared/projects/2621_eb3in1_2026/atelier_scrnaseq/SOURCES/fetch_functions.R` script that can be sourced when needed in all training sessions that require external data loading.

-   displayed below for educational purpose and not evaluated in this template. It will be **sourced** from the script cited above. 

::: {.callout-note style="background: lightblue"}

Both functions return the complete **local** (ie, user-based) path to the downloaded/copied file, so that it can be then used to load the data.

:::

- Remote from Zenodo :

```{r}
#| label: data_dl_zenofunc
#| filename: data_dl_zenofunc
#| eval: false

## ZENODO : Downloads the requested file_name to the provided local_path, 
## and returns the local position. 'force' forces the download despite 
## a local version already exists.
zenodo_get_data <- function(file_name = NULL, zenodo_id = NULL, local_path = NULL, force = FALSE) {
  ## Checks
  if (is.null(file_name)) stop("A file name to retrieve is required !")
  if (is.null(zenodo_id)) stop("A Zenodo ID is required !")
  if (is.null(local_path)) stop("A local path to store the file is required !")
  if (!is.logical(force)) stop("'force' should be TRUE or FALSE !")
  
  ## Build future local file path
  local_file <- paste0(local_path, "/", file_name)
  
  if (file.exists(local_file)) {
    message("The requested file to retrieve from Zenodo [", zenodo_id, "] already exists in [", local_path, "] !")
    if (!force) {
      message("'force' is set to 'FALSE' : nothing will be downloaded.")
      ## Nothing done : return local_file
      return(local_file)
    }
  }
  
  ## Retrieve data
  remote_file <- paste0("https://zenodo.org/records/", zenodo_id, "/files/", file_name)
  download.file(url = remote_file, destfile = local_file)
  
  ## Print and return local path
  message("Downloaded to [", local_file, "]")
  return(local_file)
}

```

- Locally from a backup :

```{r}
#| label: data_dl_locfunc
#| filename: data_dl_locfunc
#| eval: false

## BACKUP : Copies the requested backup_file to the provided local_path, 
## and returns the local position. 'force' forces the copy despite a local 
## version already exists.
backup_get_data <- function(backup_file = NULL, local_path = NULL, force = FALSE) {
  ## Checks
  if (is.null(backup_file)) stop("A backup file to retrieve is required !")
  if (is.null(local_path)) stop("A local path to store the file is required !")
  if (!is.logical(force)) stop("'force' should be TRUE or FALSE !")
  if (!file.exists(backup_file)) stop("Provided [", backup_file, "] does not exist !")
  
  ## Build future local file path
  local_file <- paste0(local_path, "/", basename(backup_file))
  
  if (file.exists(local_file)) {
    message("The requested file to retrieve already exists in [", local_path, "] !")
    if (!force) {
      message("'force' is set to 'FALSE' : nothing will be downloaded.")
      ## Nothing done : return local_file
      return(local_file)
    }
  }
  
  ## Retrieve data
  file.copy(from = backup_file,to = local_file)
  
  ## Print and return local path
  message("Copied to [", local_file, "]")
  return(local_file)
}

```

#### The remote way

:::{.callout-important}

[**[ABANDONED]**]{style="color:red"}

_(I just keep this section in case next year Zenodo will be reliable again)_

> The data we will work on is hosted on a [Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/records/14034221){target="_blank"} repository.<br> 
We will retrieve it thanks to its corresponding Zenodo ID (14034221).

```{r}
#| label: zenodo_dl_10x
#| filename: zenodo_dl_10x
#| eval: false

## Set the zenodo ID as a variable
zenodo_id <- "14034221" # <1>

## Download the requested files locally, return their user-based paths

### The 10X MTX file
matrix_mtx_file <- zenodo_get_data(
  file_name = "matrix.mtx.gz",  # <2>
  zenodo_id = zenodo_id,  # <1>
  local_path = input_dir,  # <3>
  force = TRUE) # <4>

### The 10X features metadata
features_file <- zenodo_get_data(
  file_name = "features.tsv.gz", 
  zenodo_id = zenodo_id, 
  local_path = input_dir, 
  force = TRUE)

### The 10X barcodes metadata
barcodes_file <- zenodo_get_data(
  file_name = "barcodes.tsv.gz", 
  zenodo_id = zenodo_id, 
  local_path = input_dir, 
  force = TRUE)

```

1. `zenodo_id` : The ID of the Zenodo repository
2. `file_name` : The name of the file we want to retrieve
3. `local_path` : The local path where we want the downloaded data 
to be stored. Here, it is the `input_dir` we previously defined !
4. `force` : if `TRUE`, attempts to download the file even if a local copy
already exists.

:::

# Example of code embedding and wrapping

> *Here is an example of a chunk containing a copy of a function (for display purpose) that is supposed to be sourced from this QMD script.*<br>Example of code chunk filenaming is provided.<br>Examples of code annotation are provided, to explain function parameters, and some condition testing.<br>*A small CSS hack was written to slightly move the "code-copy" button so that it does not interfere with the earliest annotations in the upper-right corner of the chunk*

## Functions

### SoupX helper function {#soupx-helper-function}

> This function was written to ease the use of SoupX on a Seurat object.<br>In practice, this code is already available in a separate script `soupX_auto.R` that will be **sourced**. It is just displayed here for educational purpose.<br>It was tested on `SoupX` = 1.6.2 with `igraph` = 1.5.1, `Seurat` = 4.4.0, 5.1.0

```{r}
#| label: soupx_func
#| filename: soupx_func
#| eval: false

SoupX_auto <- function(scmat_filt = NULL, # <1>
                       scmat_raw = NULL,  # <2>
                       soupQuantile = 0.9,  # <3>
                       contaminationRange = c(.01, .8),  # <4>
                       soupRange = c(0,100),  # <5>
                       return_object = FALSE,  # <6>
                       doPlot = FALSE) { # <7>
  
  ## Checks
  if(is.null(scmat_filt)) {
    stop('A filtered count matrix is required !') # <8>
  }
  
  if(is.null(scmat_raw)) {
    message('No unfiltered raw counts matrix provided. Estimation will be based on filtered matrix only.') # <9>
  }
  
  ## If no raw matrix
  if (is.null(scmat_raw)) { # <10>
    spChanRaw <- SoupX::SoupChannel( # <10>
      tod = scmat_filt,  # <10>
      toc = scmat_filt,  # <10>
      calcSoupProfile = FALSE) # <10>
    sc_rowsum <- sparseMatrixStats::rowSums2(scmat_filt) # <10>
    spProf <- data.frame( # <10>
      row.names = rownames(scmat_filt),  # <10>
      est = sc_rowsum/sum(scmat_filt),  # <10>
      counts = sc_rowsum) # <10>
    spChan <- SoupX::setSoupProfile(spChanRaw, spProf) # <10>
  } else { # <11>
    spChan <- SoupX::SoupChannel( # <11>
      tod = scmat_raw,  # <11>
      toc = scmat_filt,  # <11>
      calcSoupProfile = FALSE) # <11>
    if (min(spChan$nDropUMIs) > max(soupRange)) stop( # <11>
      'Minimum found counts per barcode is : ',  # <11>
      min(spChan$nDropUMIs),  # <11>
      ', which is smaller than the upper bound of soupRange !', # <11>
      ' Please increase soupRange max !') # <11>
    spChan <- SoupX::estimateSoup(sc = spChan,  # <11>
                                  soupRange = soupRange) # <11>
  } # <11>
  ## Display Top 20 contributing genes
  if (!return_object) {
    cat('\nSoup-contributing features (Top 20) :\n')
    print(knitr::kable(head(
      spChan$soupProfile[order(spChan$soupProfile$est, 
                               decreasing = TRUE), ], 
      n = 20)))
  }
  ## Quick clustering needed
  spClust <- scran::quickCluster(scmat_filt, method = "igraph")
  ## Adding clusters to the SoupChannel object
  spChan <- SoupX::setClusters(sc = spChan, clusters = spClust)
  ## Estimating soup
  sX <- SoupX::autoEstCont(sc = spChan, 
                           doPlot = doPlot, 
                           tfidfMin = 1, 
                           soupQuantile = soupQuantile, 
                           maxMarkers = 100, 
                           contaminationRange = contaminationRange, 
                           rhoMaxFDR = .2, 
                           priorRho = .05, 
                           priorRhoStdDev = .1, 
                           forceAccept = FALSE)
  
  ## Removing soup (adjusting counts)
  if(return_object) {
    cat('Counts BEFORE SoupX : ', sum(scmat_filt), '\n')
    scmat_soupx <- SoupX::adjustCounts(
      sX, 
      method = 'subtraction', 
      roundToInt = TRUE, 
      tol = .001, 
      pCut = .01)
    cat('Counts AFTER SoupX : ', sum(scmat_soupx), '\n')
    rm(scmat_filt)
    return(scmat_soupx)
  } else return(sX$fit$rhoEst)
}

```

1.  `scmat_filt` : (sparse)matrix corresponding to an empty droplets -filtered count matrix
2.  `scmat_raw` : (sparse)matrix corresponding to an NON- empty droplets -filtered count matrix
3.  `soupQuantile`, `contaminationRange` : see `?SoupX::autoEstCont`
4.  `contaminationRange` : range of the *expected* soup proportion
5.  `soupRange` : estimate soup fraction from features with total reads comprised in this range of counts (only used when `scmat_raw != NULL`)
6.  `return_object` : if `TRUE`, return the "unsouped" `Seurat` object ; if `FALSE`, only perform soup estimation and return the estimated proportion value (rho)
7.  `doPlot` : Perform the SoupX estimation plot (rho distribution)
8.  Check if a filtered matrix is provided
9.  Check if an unfiltered matrix is provided
10. Handle the worst case of the unfiltered matrix not provided
11. Handle the better case of the unfiltered matrix provided

# SeuratObject RDS naming convention

>At the end of each training session, or for intermediate steps that may take
quite some time to reproduce in case of error, the modified SeuratObject is
saved as a compressed RDS.

A proposal for a naming convention :

<CENTER>**[06]{style="color:blue"}\_TD3A\_S5\_[LogNorm]{style="color:red"}\_[12508]{style="color:green"}.[4035]{style="color:brown"}.RDS**</CENTER>

-   [**06**]{style="color:blue"} : The ordered step number
-   **TD3A** : The sample name (fixed)
-   **S5** : To recall the RDS contains a SeuratObject v5
-   [**LogNorm**]{style="color:red"} : The step name
-   [**12508**]{style="color:green"} : The number of features at the current step
-   [**4035**]{style="color:brown"} : The number of barcodes at the current step

And here is a chunk to describe how it is real-time generated :

```{r}
#| label: save_rds
#| filename: save_rds
#| eval: false

## Save our Seurat object (rich naming)
out_name <- paste0(
              output_dir, "/", paste(
                c("06", 
                  Seurat::Project(sobj), 
                  "S5", 
                  "LogNorm",
                  paste(
                    dim(sobj), 
                    collapse = '.')
                ), collapse = "_"),
              ".RDS")

## Check
print(out_name)

## Write on disk
saveRDS(object = sobj, 
        file = out_name)
```

::: {.callout-note style="background: lightblue"}
## NOTE 1

Some steps require additional information. By example, for **scaling**, the number of HVGs is added (abbreviated in "`2k`").
:::

::: {.callout-note style="background: lightblue"}
## NOTE 2

The entirety of the intermediate SeuratObjects saved as RDS is available here :

`/shared/projects/2621_eb3in1_2026/atelier_scrnaseq/DATA_BACKUP/INTERMEDIATE`
